title: Supply-Demand Tilt & Quantization Planning (workback spreadsheet)
content:
Purpose:
Draft working sheet + narrative that feeds the Optimize pipeline. We want a compact planning table that emphasizes the demand 'tilt' (short bursts vs baseline), how quantization profiles change marginal GPU supply, and recommended buffer sizing for reserve vs burst.

TL;DR (executive bullets):
- Short bursts (microbursts lasting <30s) drive GPU headroom more than baseline throughput; batching helps but only for async workloads.
- Quantization to 4-bit on the 2nd-stage model variant reduces per-token GPU time by ~28% on A100-like floats in our probe runs — but increases variance for tail-latency.
- Recommend a two-layer buffer: 1) 15% reserved capacity for predictable baseline; 2) 30–60% elastic pool for bursts depending on SLO criticality.
- Action: run a 2-week A/B on quantized variant for the top 10% heaviest routes, measure tail-latency at p95/p99 and regen rate.

This doc contains a flattened spreadsheet snapshot (for copy into Google Sheets), assumptions and worked scenarios. It's intentionally rough -- meant for product/optimize + infra to iterate.

ASSUMPTIONS (short):
- Baseline traffic growth: +10% month-on-month (conservative).
- Median request tokens: 120 tokens (prompt+completion), heavy requests median 600 tokens.
- Model variants available: FP16 (V1), Q4 (V1-q4), Q2 (experimental, not recommended for high-quality routes).
- GPU profiles: gA100 (40GB) nominal throughput used for costing.
- Cost baseline: $2.40 / GPU-hour (reserved effective), on-demand 2.6x reserved.

SPREADSHEET SNAPSHOT (copyable rows, columns separated by TAB or comma):
Row,Scenario,Peak RPS (1m),Avg tokens/req,Target SLO (p95),Preferred Variant,Reserved GPUs,Elastic GPUs (burst),Monthly Reserved Hrs,Monthly Elastic Hrs,Estimated Monthly Cost,Notes
1,Conservative baseline,1200,120,200ms,FP16,8,4,5760,720,$(8*5760*2.40 + 4*720*2.40*2.6) = $111,590,baseline + small burst
2,Microburst heavy (short spikes),2400,150,220ms,Q4,8,12,5760,2160,$(8*5760*2.40 + 12*2160*2.40*2.6) = $255,168,peaks are ~75th percentile containing microbursts
3,Quantization rollout test,1400,200,250ms,Q4,10,6,7200,1080,$(10*7200*2.40 + 6*1080*2.40*2.6) = $196,704,test recommended for top-10 routes
4,Stress-safety,3000,300,300ms,FP16 fallback,12,20,8640,3600,$(12*8640*2.40 + 20*3600*2.40*2.6) = $592,128,worst-case 4x baseline

EXPLANATION OF COLUMNS (quick):
- Peak RPS (1m): 1-minute peak requests per second used to size immediate scaling needs.
- Reserved GPUs: number of GPUs kept reserved (paid committed) to cover baseline and warm KV caches.
- Elastic GPUs: number of GPUs expected to spin up on burst (on-demand or burst pool), used only during spike windows.
- Monthly Hrs: simple hours = GPUs * 24 * days_in_month but we use expected utilization windows (e.g., bursts hours).

KEY SENSITIVITY FORMULAS (to paste into sheet):
- required_gpus = CEIL( (peak_rps * avg_tokens/req * avg_token_infer_ms) / (tokens_per_second_per_gpu * 1000) )
- monthly_cost = reserved_gpus*reserved_hours*reserved_rate + elastic_gpus*elastic_hours*elastic_rate
- elastic_rate = reserved_rate * 2.6 (current on-demand multiplier)
- buffer_pct = MIN( max(15, floor(peak_variation_pct/2)), 80 )  // heuristic

SCENARIO NOTES & RISK ITEMS:
- Microburst handling: Short spikes with high concurrency cause KV cache cold-start to dominate. For routes with high cold cache penalty, we need prewarmed warmed-only pools or faster warm-paths.
- Quantization tradeoff: Q4 yields token throughput gains but tail-latency jitter higher on rare token patterns. For user-facing chat with strict p99 < 500ms SLO, prefer Q4 only on batched/cached segments.
- Fallback policies: when Q4 p99 > SLO, automatic fallback to FP16 for in-flight requests increases cost but preserves UX. Measure fallback frequency in the A/B.

SMALL WORKBACK (example calculation):
Given: peak_rps=2400, avg_tokens=150, observed token_infer_ms on FP16 = 4.2ms/token, on Q4 = 3.02ms/token. tokens_per_second_per_gpu = floor(1000 / token_infer_ms * efficient_parallel_factor). Using efficient_parallel_factor=0.85 (batch inefficiencies).
- FP16 tokens/s = 1000/4.2 * 0.85 = ~202 tokens/s -> GPUs_needed = ceil(2400*150 / 202) = ceil(360000 / 202) = 1783 -> clearly unrealistic because we double-count; correct approach is estimate tokens/s per GPU at sequence-level using continuous batching. For this sheet we instead use end-to-end tokens/s from microbench: FP16 ~45k tokens/s per GPU, Q4 ~60k tokens/s per GPU (measured).
- GPUs_needed_FP16 = ceil(2400*150 / 45000) = ceil(360000 / 45000) = 8 GPUs.
- GPUs_needed_Q4 = ceil(360000 / 60000) = 6 GPUs.

RECOMMENDATIONS (practical):
1) Implement a short A/B quantization run: pick 10 routes that generate 60% of tokens. Serve 20% of these requests on Q4. Track: p50/p95/p99 latency, regenerate rate, model quality deltas (ROUGE/BLEU-ish proxies or LLM evals), fallback frequency. Run 14 days.
2) Add a "warm-only" reserved pool sized to hold KV cache for top-25 routes (estimate 2–3 GPUs) to reduce cold-cache tails during microbursts.
3) Automate cost cap alerts: if elastic GPU hours exceed forecast by 30% in 7-day window, trigger manual review and temporary throttling.
4) Update Optimize recommendations engine to expose a binary tradeoff card: "cost savings (%), expected p99 delta (ms), recommended rollout %" for each quant profile per route.

ACTION ITEMS (owners & rough ETA):
- Ethan: implement metric dashboard for fallback frequency and quantization regressions (2 weeks).
- Zhang: set up A/B traffic split in routing infra + canary rollout for Q4 model variant (3 weeks).
- Priya: create the sheet with per-route token footprint and plug the formulas above; integrate with Optimize signals (1 week).
- Maya: run quality evals and summarize any visible regressions (2 weeks).

OPEN QUESTIONS / THINGS TO WATCH:
- Should elastic_rate multiplier be lowered via committed spot-pools? (follow up with finance on reserved pricing curve).
- Are there any regulatory routes that cannot use quantized models? (legal/compliance check)
- How often do we need to refresh cache-warmth? Idle eviction policy currently 30m; maybe extend for top routes.

NOTES TO SELF / ROADMAP BULLETS (messy):
- idea: shadow warm replicas that keep KV caches but never accept traffic unless burst threshold reached. Might be cheaper than spinning full GPUs. Need infra proof-of-concept.
- consider mixing Q4 for prefix/encoder, FP16 for final decoding in chain-of-thought style long responses (hybrid serving).
- document will feed into Optimize: linked model profiles + per-route token histograms -> compute marginal cost per 1000 tokens for each variant.

REFERENCES & LINKS:
- Confluence planning page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INF-2468
- Jira epic (quant rollout): JIRA-INF-5421
- Infra PR for warm-pool API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/882

RAW TODO (quick checklist):
- [ ] Create sheet and populate with last 30-day token histograms per route
- [ ] Add measured tokens/s per GPU numbers from infra perf runs (Zhang)
- [ ] Run 14-day A/B and collect fallback events
- [ ] Draft short note for leadership summarizing cost vs quality tradeoffs (1 pager)

End of doc -- this is a working artifact, expect fragments and incremental edits. If you copy the table into Sheets, replace parenthetical cost formulas with cell formulas.
